Solve the supplied rule-constrained task. Return short JSON matching the response schema. Jointly propose an executable rule sketch and any entity/group/usage interface. Do not omit exceptions. A compiled unit needs a source link to a binding or query; unlisted units remain residual. Do not claim unsupported text is compiled. program.kind is expression, connector, or unsupported. For expression body use bindings [{name,value,type,source}], query {op,args}, source_links {unit:[node]}. Types: integer, rational (decimal string), scalar. Connectors also accept relation A string input uses type scalar, not string. Expression names start with n_ for numbers, s_ for strings, b_ for booleans; source IDs such as s0 are provenance only. An expression body requires bindings, query and source_links. Do not copy every source sentence into bindings; bind only public literals needed by an executable query. If no faithful query is available, use unsupported with body {} and keep the native answer separate. {columns,rows,closed}, amount (one value,unit,owner,period,lineage,stage object), amounts (a list of these objects), allowance_bank (entries key,balance,policy,order_observable), resource_key, slot_list. Do not invent entity witnesses or guess allocation policies. A variable is {var:name}. Operators: if,and,or,not,eq,ne,lt,le,add,sub,min,max,scale (literal constant first), divide_constant (literal denominator), array,pair,object,concat. No arbitrary code. Bind observed values and rule constants from public source units. Node names are query and binding:NAME. Use unsupported with empty body when faithful executable translation is unavailable. Always give your task answer in answer; this fixed fallback has no stability certificate. Interface proposals may describe a source-linked join/group/map/reduce graph, but never use source IDs or answers as routing features. Each interfaces entry has exactly fields (allowed semantic field names), graph (connector DSL), and bindings (same source-linked binding format); use [] when unavailable. A connector body has bindings,candidates,source_links,project; optional query wraps its result. Projection modes: identity, amount_value (one Amount), amount_values (list of Amount), entailment_label (Boolean claim to binary Entailment/Contradiction). A wrapper query reads n_result/b_result/s_result, or n_result_0,n_result_1,... for numeric list results. Never bind these output names as public inputs. An expression variable may remain unbound only if public text itself declares its full finite domain: Boolean b_NAME = true/false.; Integer n_NAME in [integers] = integer.; or Enum s_NAME in [strings] = string. Keep its untranslated source unit residual. Other unread text has unknown scope; do not invent domains or missing rules. Do not store case amounts or names as reusable skill constants. Answer contract: "Entailment" or "Contradiction"
Executable contract clarification: bindings contain only extracted public inputs and rule constants; never put an answer object or a program into a scalar string. JSON text in a string is not executable. A source identifier such as s0 is provenance metadata, never a boolean or a variable. Read a bound input with {"var":"name"}. and/or/not take booleans; comparisons return booleans. Expression binding names use n_ for integer/rational, s_ for strings, b_ for booleans; numeric references must name n_ slots, string keys s_ slots, boolean references b_ slots. Choose op before writing args. The maximum expression depth is16; use concise expressions. The root query must return the native task result: a numeric operation for Airline, an if producing an Entailment/Contradiction string for SARA, and an object operation producing EC/EV for OpenExempt. OpenExempt EC values are arrays of literal legal citation strings containing §. EV values are arrays of object operations with exactly citation (a literal citation string) and claim_value (a numeric expression). if has exactly [boolean condition, complete true branch, complete false branch]; both branches must type check. add/sub/min/max/lt/le take exact numbers. scale is [literal integer, numeric expression]; divide_constant is [numeric expression, nonzero literal integer]. Arrays use {op:array,args:[...]}; pair is [string key,value expression]; object takes pair operations as its args, never raw JSON fields. source_links maps current unit IDs to existing node names: query or binding:NAME (connector:i for connectors). Use actual cited lines for each input; cite all rule/exception lines needed for the query. Every scalar string must be an exact nonempty substring of its cited unit, never a paraphrase. A boolean binding is allowed only when its cited unit explicitly contains the standalone literal true or false. Assumptions, inferred states and absent information are not boolean inputs. Express rule conditions using comparisons on quoted inputs; otherwise leave the translation unsupported. Do not mark unrelated units compiled. Omitted units remain residual. Unknown semantics must remain unsupported, never replaced with a guessed rule. Interfaces use only the seven documented connector operators, or []. The complete example below illustrates syntax using an invented task. Its answer definition and facts belong only to that invented task. Read the CURRENT public question to determine all required components of its answer. Compile the current public task afresh.
[{"public_text":"Age: 25.\nThe claim is Entailment if age is at least 21, otherwise Contradiction.","proposal":{"program":{"kind":"expression","body":{"bindings":[{"name":"n_age","type":"integer","value":25,"source":"s0"},{"name":"n_threshold","type":"integer","value":21,"source":"s1"}],"query":{"op":"if","args":[{"op":"le","args":[{"var":"n_threshold"},{"var":"n_age"}]},"Entailment","Contradiction"]},"source_links":{"s0":["query"],"s1":["query"]}}},"answer":"Entailment","compiled_units":["s0","s1"],"unsupported_units":[],"interfaces":[]}}]
The SARA task is to evaluate the exact claim supplied as query under the supplied rules and facts. Entailment means that claim follows; Contradiction means that claim is false in this binary task. The query is the proposition to classify, not an additional fact. Do not substitute another legal question.

[s0] §3306. Definitions
[s1] (a) Employer
[s2]     (1) In general
[s3]     The term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who-
[s4]         (A) during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages of $1,500 or more, or
[s5]         (B) on each of some 10 days during the calendar year or during the preceding calendar year, each day being in a different calendar week, employed at least one individual in employment for some portion of the day.
[s6]     For purposes of this paragraph, there shall not be taken into account any wages paid to, or employment of, an employee performing domestic services referred to in paragraph (3).
[s7]     (2) Agricultural labor
[s8]     In the case of agricultural labor, the term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who-
[s9]         (A) during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages of $20,000 or more for agricultural labor, or
[s10]         (B) on each of some 10 days during the calendar year or during the preceding calendar year, each day being in a different calendar week, employed at least 5 individuals in employment in agricultural labor for some portion of the day.
[s11]     (3) Domestic service
[s12]     In the case of domestic service in a private home, local college club, or local chapter of a college fraternity or sorority, the term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages in cash of $1,000 or more for such service.
[s13]     (4) Special rule
[s14]     A person treated as an employer under paragraph (3) shall not be treated as an employer with respect to wages paid for any service other than domestic service referred to in paragraph (3) unless such person is treated as an employer under paragraph (1) or (2) with respect to such other service.
[s15] (b) Wages
[s16] For purposes of this chapter, the term "wages" means all remuneration for employment, including the cash value of all remuneration (including benefits) paid in any medium other than cash; except that such term shall not include-
[s17]     (1) that part of the remuneration which, after remuneration (other than remuneration referred to in the succeeding paragraphs of this subsection) equal to $7,000 with respect to employment has been paid to an individual by an employer during any calendar year, is paid to such individual by such employer during such calendar year;
[s18]     (2) the amount of any payment (including any amount paid by an employer for insurance or annuities, or into a fund, to provide for any such payment) made to, or on behalf of, an employee or any of his dependents under a plan or system established by an employer which makes provision for his employees generally (or for his employees generally and their dependents) or for a class or classes of his employees (or for a class or classes of his employees and their dependents), on account of-
[s19]         (A) sickness or accident disability, or
[s20]         (C) death;
[s21]     (7) remuneration paid in any medium other than cash to an employee for service not in the course of the employer's trade or business;
[s22]     (10) any payment or series of payments by an employer to an employee or any of his dependents which is paid-
[s23]         (A) upon or after the termination of an employee's employment relationship because of (i) death, or (ii) retirement for disability, and
[s24]         (B) under a plan established by the employer which makes provision for his employees generally or a class or classes of his employees (or for such employees or class or classes of employees and their dependents),
[s25]     other than any such payment or series of payments which would have been paid if the employee's employment relationship had not been so terminated;
[s26]     (11) remuneration for agricultural labor paid in any medium other than cash;
[s27]     (15) any payment made by an employer to a survivor or the estate of a former employee after the calendar year in which such employee died;
[s28] (c) Employment
[s29] For purposes of this chapter, the term "employment" means any service, of whatever nature,
[s30]     (A) performed by an employee for the person employing him, irrespective of the citizenship or residence of either, within the United States, and
[s31]     (B) performed outside the United States (except in a contiguous country with which the United States has an agreement relating to unemployment compensation) by a citizen of the United States as an employee of an American employer, except-
[s32]     (1) agricultural labor unless-
[s33]         (A) such labor is performed for a person who-
[s34]             (i) during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid remuneration in cash of $20,000 or more to individuals employed in agricultural labor (including labor performed by an alien referred to in subparagraph (B)), or
[s35]             (ii) on each of some 10 days during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year, each day being in a different calendar week, employed in agricultural labor (including labor performed by an alien referred to in subparagraph (B)) for some portion of the day (whether or not at the same moment of time) 5 or more individuals; and
[s36]         (B) such labor is not agricultural labor performed by an individual who is an alien admitted to the United States to perform agricultural labor pursuant to sections 214(c) and 101(a)(15)(H) of the Immigration and Nationality Act.
[s37]     (2) domestic service in a private home, local college club, or local chapter of a college fraternity or sorority unless performed for a person who paid cash remuneration of $1,000 or more to individuals employed in such domestic service in the calendar year or the preceding calendar year;
[s38]     (5) 
[s39]         (A) service performed by an individual in the employ of his son, daughter, or spouse;
[s40]         (B) service performed by a child under the age of 21 in the employ of his father or mother;
[s41]     (6) service performed in the employ of the United States Government
[s42]     (7) service performed in the employ of a State, or any political subdivision thereof.
[s43]     (10)
[s44]         (A) service performed in the employ of a school, college, or university, if such service is performed
[s45]             (i) by a student who is enrolled and is regularly attending classes at such school, college, or university, or
[s46]             (ii) by the spouse of such a student, or
[s47]         (B) service performed in the employ of a hospital, if such service is performed by a patient of such hospital;
[s48]     (11) service performed in the employ of a foreign government (including service as a consular or other officer or employee or a nondiplomatic representative);
[s49]     (13) service performed as a student nurse in the employ of a hospital or a nurses' training school by an individual who is enrolled and is regularly attending classes in a nurses' training school;
[s50]     (16) service performed in the employ of an international organization;
[s51]     (21) service performed by a person committed to a penal institution.
[s52] Alice was paid $200 in 2017 for services performed in a hospital. Alice was committed to a psychiatric hospital from January 24, 2015 to May 5th, 2019.
[s53] Section 3306(c)(21) applies to Alice's employment situation in 2017.
Exact claim to classify (verbatim public query): "Section 3306(c)(21) applies to Alice's employment situation in 2017."
